description: Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani is a beloved Indian classic known for its incredibly rich, creamy tomato-based sauce. Tender pieces of marinated chicken are simmered in this luxurious gravy, offering a perfect balance of sweet, tangy, and mildly spicy flavors. It's a comforting and flavorful dish that truly embodies the heart of Indian cuisine.

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine chicken pieces with yogurt, 1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste, turmeric powder, red chili powder, garam masala, and salt. Mix well to coat the chicken. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or preferably 2-4 hours for best flavor.

instructions.title: Cook the Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 1 tablespoon butter and 1 tablespoon oil in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces and cook in batches until browned on all sides and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes per batch. Remove chicken from the pan and set aside.

instructions.title: Prepare the Sauce Base
instructions.text: In the same pan, melt 2 tablespoons butter over medium heat. Add the finely chopped onion and sauté until translucent and lightly golden, about 5-7 minutes. Add 1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant.

instructions.title: Simmer the Tomato Gravy
instructions.text: Stir in the crushed tomatoes, soaked cashews (drained), and sugar. Bring the mixture to a simmer, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 10-12 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and tomatoes to soften. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.

instructions.title: Blend and Refine the Sauce
instructions.text: Carefully transfer the tomato mixture to a blender or use an immersion blender to blend until completely smooth. Pass the blended sauce through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pan for an extra smooth, restaurant-style consistency. Discard any solids left in the sieve.

instructions.title: Finish and Combine
instructions.text: Return the smooth sauce to medium-low heat. Stir in the remaining 1 tablespoon butter, crushed Kasuri Methi, and heavy cream. Add the cooked chicken pieces to the sauce. Simmer gently for another 5-7 minutes, allowing the chicken to absorb the rich flavors of the makhani sauce. Taste and adjust salt or sugar if needed.

instructions.title: Serve Hot
instructions.text: Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro. Serve your authentic Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani hot with basmati rice, naan bread, or roti. Enjoy this creamy, flavorful Indian delight!

tips: For an even richer flavor, marinate the chicken overnight. The longer it marinates, the more tender and flavorful it will be.
Using Kashmiri red chili powder gives a beautiful vibrant red color without adding too much heat. If unavailable, use regular red chili powder sparingly.
Always pass the sauce through a sieve after blending for that truly smooth, restaurant-quality texture. Don't skip this step for authentic Murgh Makhani.
article:
Unveiling the Silky Secret: Mastering Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani for Your Indian Lunch

Few dishes capture the heart and palate quite like Butter Chicken, known in India as Murgh Makhani. This iconic Indian lunch recipe has transcended borders, becoming a global sensation celebrated for its incredibly rich, creamy, and subtly spiced tomato-based sauce, enveloping succulent pieces of tender chicken. If you’ve ever dreamed of recreating that restaurant-quality experience in your own kitchen, you’re in the right place. Get ready to embark on a culinary journey that will transform your midday meal into an extraordinary feast.

## What is Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani?

At its core, Murgh Makhani translates to "chicken with butter," a name that beautifully encapsulates the essence of this beloved dish. Originating in Delhi, India, in the post-partition era, Butter Chicken quickly rose to prominence thanks to its innovative use of a creamy, mildly spiced tomato gravy. The story often traces back to the Moti Mahal restaurant, where leftover tandoori chicken was simmered in a rich tomato sauce with butter and cream, creating a dish that was both comforting and luxurious.

What makes Butter Chicken so irresistible is its masterful balance of flavors. The tang of tomatoes is mellowed by the sweetness of cream and a touch of sugar, while aromatic spices like garam masala, cardamom, and fenugreek (kasuri methi) add depth without overwhelming heat. The chicken, typically marinated in yogurt and spices before cooking, emerges incredibly tender, soaking up all the glorious flavors of the sauce. It's a testament to simple ingredients coming together to create something truly magical, making it a fantastic Butter Chicken recipe to master at home.

## Ingredients You Need

Crafting the perfect Murgh Makhani starts with selecting quality ingredients. While the list might seem extensive, each component plays a crucial role in building the dish's signature flavor profile.

**For the Chicken Marinade:**
*   1.5 lbs boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breasts, cut into 1-inch cubes
*   1/2 cup plain full-fat yogurt
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste (equal parts fresh ginger and garlic, crushed)
*   1 tablespoon lemon juice
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder (Kashmiri chili powder for color and mild heat)
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   1/2 teaspoon salt

**For the Makhani Sauce:**
*   2 tablespoons ghee or unsalted butter, plus more for garnish
*   1 large onion, finely chopped
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 (28-ounce) can crushed tomatoes or tomato puree
*   1/4 cup raw cashews (soaked in hot water for 15-20 minutes, optional but recommended for richness)
*   1/2 cup water or chicken broth
*   1/2 cup heavy cream, plus more for garnish
*   1 tablespoon Kasuri Methi (dried fenugreek leaves), crushed
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder
*   1 teaspoon sugar (or to taste, to balance acidity)
*   Salt to taste
*   Fresh cilantro, chopped (for garnish)

## Step-by-Step Instructions

Follow these steps carefully to create a Butter Chicken that rivals your favorite Indian restaurant.

1.  **Marinate the Chicken:** In a large bowl, combine the cubed chicken with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, lemon juice, red chili powder, turmeric, garam masala, and salt. Mix thoroughly to coat all the chicken pieces. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or ideally 2-4 hours, to allow the flavors to penetrate deeply.
2.  **Cook the Chicken:** Heat 1 tablespoon of ghee or butter in a large skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken in a single layer, working in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding the pan. Cook until browned on all sides and mostly cooked through, about 5-7 minutes per batch. Remove the cooked chicken and set aside.
3.  **Prepare the Sauce Base:** In the same pan, add the remaining 1 tablespoon of ghee or butter. Add the finely chopped onions and sauté until translucent and softened, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in the ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant.
4.  **Add Tomatoes and Spices:** Pour in the crushed tomatoes. If using soaked cashews, drain them and add them to the pan now. Stir in the garam masala, red chili powder, and salt. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 10-15 minutes, allowing the sauce to thicken slightly and the raw tomato flavor to cook out. You'll notice the oil starting to separate around the edges.
5.  **Blend the Sauce:** Carefully transfer the cooked sauce mixture (including cashews, if used) to a blender. Add 1/2 cup of water or chicken broth. Blend until the sauce is perfectly smooth and creamy. For an extra silky texture, you can pass the blended sauce through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pan.
6.  **Finish the Makhani Sauce:** Return the smooth sauce to the pan over medium-low heat. Stir in the heavy cream, the remaining 1 tablespoon of butter, and the sugar. Bring to a gentle simmer, stirring constantly to prevent scorching.
7.  **Combine and Serve:** Add the cooked chicken pieces back into the simmering sauce. Crush the Kasuri Methi between your palms and stir it into the dish. Let it simmer for another 5-10 minutes, allowing the chicken to finish cooking and to absorb the rich flavors of the sauce. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed. Garnish generously with fresh cilantro and a swirl of extra cream or a small pat of butter before serving. Your homemade Butter Chicken is ready!

## Pro Tips for the Best Results

Achieving truly spectacular Butter Chicken often comes down to a few key techniques and considerations.

*   **Marination is Key:** Don't skimp on marination time. The yogurt tenderizes the chicken, and the spices infuse it with flavor, ensuring every bite is succulent and delicious. Overnight marination is ideal.
*   **Blend Until Silky Smooth:** The hallmark of an authentic Murgh Makhani is its velvety texture. Blend the sauce thoroughly until no lumps remain. For the ultimate smoothness, pass it through a fine-mesh sieve.
*   **Kasuri Methi Magic:** Dried fenugreek leaves (Kasuri Methi) are non-negotiable for authentic flavor. They impart a unique, slightly bitter, and aromatic depth that can't be replicated. Always crush them between your palms before adding to release their essential oils.
*   **Balance Flavors:** Taste your sauce! A touch of sugar helps balance the acidity of the tomatoes, while a little extra salt or a squeeze of lemon juice can brighten the flavors. Don't be afraid to adjust.
*   **Resting Time:** Like many stews and curries, Butter Chicken often tastes even better the next day as the flavors have more time to meld and deepen. This makes it an excellent make-ahead option for your Indian lunch.

## Serving Suggestions

This rich and flavorful Butter Chicken pairs perfectly with a variety of Indian sides, making for a truly satisfying meal.

Serve it hot with fluffy Basmati rice or fragrant Jeera rice (cumin rice) to soak up every last drop of the exquisite sauce. For an authentic experience, scoop up the creamy sauce with warm, buttery naan bread, soft roti, or flaky paratha. A cooling side of cucumber raita (yogurt with cucumber and spices) or a simple green salad provides a refreshing contrast to the richness of the curry. Don't forget a wedge of lemon for an optional squeeze of brightness.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Butter Chicken is undeniably delicious, there are many ways to adapt this recipe to suit different preferences or dietary needs.

*   **Vegetarian Options:** Easily transform this into a vegetarian Murgh Makhani by replacing the chicken with paneer (Indian cottage cheese), firm tofu, or a medley of vegetables like cauliflower, peas, and potatoes. Adjust cooking times accordingly.
*   **Cream Alternatives:** For a dairy-free version, use full-fat coconut milk or a homemade cashew cream (soaked and blended cashews with water) instead of heavy cream. Ensure your butter is also plant-based.
*   **Spice Level:** Adjust the amount of red chili powder to your liking. For extra heat, add a pinch of cayenne pepper or a finely chopped green chili during the onion sautéing step.
*   **Smoking (Dhungaar):** For an authentic smoky flavor reminiscent of tandoor-cooked chicken, try the "dhungaar" method. Heat a small piece of charcoal until red hot, place it in a small heatproof bowl inside the pot with the finished curry, drizzle a teaspoon of ghee over it, and quickly cover the pot for 2-3 minutes. Remove the charcoal before serving.
*   **Grilling Chicken:** Instead of pan-frying, grill or bake the marinated chicken until cooked through and slightly charred for an extra layer of smoky flavor before adding it to the sauce.

Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani is more than just a meal; it's a culinary experience. Its exquisite balance of creamy texture, sweet and savory notes, and tender chicken makes it an unforgettable Indian lunch recipe. Whether you're a seasoned chef or a home cook, following this guide will help you create a restaurant-quality dish that will impress and delight. Embrace the warmth and richness of this iconic Indian classic!
